title: fix(desktop): cursor track keeps its last samples (audit REC-B8)
body:
## What changed and why

The cursor froze 0.1–0.3 s before the end of every recording (audit finding **REC-B8**, [record lens B](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/blob/main/apps/documentation/src/content/docs/audits/2026-10-15/findings/record-b.md)).

Cause: at finalize, main drops cursor samples past `meta.durationMs + 250`. The samples are in **video time** (measured from `t0`, the MP4's first media sample), but `durationMs` came from the bar's **wall clock**, which only starts after `startEngine` resolves — after the thumbnail capture (150 ms sleep + play + JPEG). That gap (≥ 150 ms, typically 200–350 ms) ate the 250 ms margin, so the last samples and clicks were cut.

Fix (approved spec: `apps/documentation/src/content/docs/specs/2026-10-28-niw2-402-cursor-track-tail.md`):

- `recorder-store.ts`: a second clock, `videoClock`, starts at `firstMediaTimestamp.rendererMs` — the same `t0` the cursor track is anchored to — on `performance.now()`. It gets the same pause/resume instants as the cursor track and is read at Stop for `durationMs`. If `t0` never resolved, `durationMs` falls back to the wall clock (same as before). An `engine === handle` guard stops a late `firstMediaTimestamp` from an earlier take from leaking into the next one. The wall clock still drives the bar timer and `durationSeconds`.
- `recording-hub.ts`, `ipc.ts`, `build-cursor-track.ts`: comments only, saying `durationMs` / `maxMs` are video time.
- New `cursor-track-tail.fixture.test.ts`: uses the real 25 s fixture plus 150 ms of synthetic tail samples to pin the builder's contract. All tail samples survive when `maxMs` is video duration + margin; the old 350 ms-late clock dropped the last ~100 ms.
- Deletes audit plan 26 and its row in `plans/audit-2026-10-15/00-index.md`, and adds it to the Shipped table.

No change to IPC shape, main logic or the builder.

### Known limits (out of scope, per the spec)

- **Pause before `t0`:** a pause issued before `firstMediaTimestamp` resolves (less than one frame; the UI cannot hit it) is not applied to `videoClock`. The cursor tracker has the same limitation.
- **`durationSeconds` stays on the wall clock:** it is the floor of the wall clock (library metadata, "Saved" card), so it can be up to ~Δ (the 150–350 ms gap) shorter than the file.

## How I verified it

From `apps/kaipu-record` (pinned vitest, Node 22):

- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.test.ts`: before the fix, the new "video time" test **failed** (it got 2400, expected 2750). After the fix, 62/62 pass. The new tests cover `t0` 350 ms early, a 1 s pause, and the fallback when `t0` never resolves. The existing durationMs test now uses `rendererMs: 3000`, which is when recording starts on the fake clock.
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recording/cursor-track-tail.fixture.test.ts src/main/recording/build-cursor-track.test.ts src/shared/cursor-track.fixture.test.ts`: 10/10 pass.

From the repo root:

- `bun run check-types`: green.
- `bun run verify`: green, run twice in a row. The second run was entirely Turbo cache hits. 300 test files, 2883 tests.

I did not run the Playwright desktop E2E suite locally (CI runs it) and did not record on a real machine.

## How to test it yourself

Use a dev build (`bun run dev` in `apps/kaipu-record`).

1. Record about 5 s. Right before pressing Stop, move the pointer to a screen corner. Open the recording in the editor: the cursor should follow all the way to the last frame instead of freezing 0.1–0.3 s early.
2. Compare the last `t` in `<vault>/.kaipu/<id>.cursor.json` with the video's duration. They should be within ~50 ms (before this fix: 100–350 ms short).
3. Record with a pause in the middle. The cursor track should still line up with the video after the pause.

Refs NIW2-402
